text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- King Hussein and British Prime Minister Tony Blair discuss bilateral ties and the Middle East peace process; king refers to need to ease the suffering of the Iraqi people.
- Trial of the Jordanian soldier who shot dead seven Israeli schoolgirls resumes on Saturday; defence prepares to present its first witnesses in the session.

- Prime Minister Abdul Salam al-Majali stresses during talks with senior Tunisian officials the benefits of coordination between Arab states; Jordanian-Tunisian talks agree on the need for an investment promotion accord and setting up a joint Tunisian-Jordanian bank.
- Jordanian opposition to organise next month a solidarity conference with the Palestinians living in Arab East Jerusalem.
- King Hussein emphasises in talks in London with British Prime Minister Blair the need to activate the European role to help push forward the Middle East peace process to get it back on track.

- Opposition deputies plan to meet Prime Minister Majali to put across their viewpoint over the government's handling of preparations for the coming parliamentary elections. They also plan to protest the government's refusal to allow them to organise demonstrations to protest a tougher press and publications law.
- King Hussein says Middle East peace negotiations have reached a dead end and emphasises the need to find a way out of the impasse.
